chatops.help:
IsItDown commands

/status — every provider, worst first
/status <provider> — one provider
/history <provider> [7|30|90] — uptime over a window
/mute <provider> <30m|2h|1d> — stop alerts for a while
/unmute <provider> — start them again
/ack <provider> — say you are on it
/help — this message

cli.usage:
usage: isitdown <command>

Commands:
  watch    show the fleet from a running UI edition instance and redraw as it changes
  discover read a project's files and propose the providers it depends on
  import   read another monitoring tool's export and propose the providers it becomes

Run 'isitdown <command> --help' for its options.
cli.error.invalidInterval: --interval must be a positive number of seconds: {value}
cli.watch.usage:
usage: isitdown watch [--url <url>] [--token <token>] [--interval <seconds>]

Reads a running UI edition instance's fleet and redraws as it changes.
Read-only: this command never writes to the instance it watches.

  --url       instance to read (default: http://localhost:3000)
  --token     read-only API token (default: $API_TOKEN)
  --interval  polling fallback interval in seconds, used only while the
              live stream is unavailable (default: 30)
cli.watch.title: IsItDown watch — {url}
cli.watch.error.unauthorized: the server rejected this token (401 Unauthorized)
cli.watch.error.forbidden: this token cannot read this instance (403 Forbidden)
cli.watch.empty: No providers configured on this instance.
cli.watch.changes.heading: Recent changes
cli.discover.usage:
usage: isitdown discover [path...] [--yaml | --json]

Reads a project's files — package.json, compose files, Dockerfiles, .env,
Terraform, requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, go.mod, a hosts file — and
proposes the catalog providers it depends on, with what gave each one away.
Offline: nothing is fetched and nothing is written.

  path    files or directories to read (default: the current directory)
  --yaml  print a services: block for a Light edition config.yml
  --json  print the full result as JSON
cli.discover.none: No catalog provider found in them.
cli.discover.unmatched: Hosts no catalog entry matches — add them by url if they have a status page:
cli.discover.next: Run again with --yaml for a config.yml services: block.
cli.discover.no-files: No file discovery can read was found.
cli.import.usage:
usage: isitdown import <file> [--from <tool>] [--yaml | --json]

Reads another monitoring tool's export and proposes the providers it becomes:
probes, status pages the catalog recognises, and heartbeats for jobs that call
in — with what did not carry over and why. Offline: nothing is fetched and
nothing is written.

  file         an Uptime Kuma backup (JSON), a Gatus config.yaml, a Statping
               export (JSON) or a StatusGator board's monitor list (JSON)
  --from tool  uptimekuma, gatus, statping or statusgator (default: detected)
  --yaml       print a services: block for a Light edition config.yml
  --json       print the full result as JSON

cli.import.note.slow-is-degraded: a slow answer reads degraded here, not down
cli.import.note.cadence-raised: cadence raised to the fastest allowed
cli.import.note.cadence-lowered: cadence lowered to the slowest allowed
cli.import.reason.unsupported-method: a probe only repeats GET or HEAD
cli.import.reason.page-not-in-catalog: a status page the catalog does not know — add it by URL and detection will name its adapter
cli.import.reason.no-interval: no expected interval, so nothing could say it is late
cli.import.reason.duplicate: the same provider as an earlier monitor
cli.import.reason.invalid: would not make a valid provider
